Enicepatide (CT-388): Roche's GLP-1/GIP Biased Dual Agonist With 22.7% Phase 2 Weight Loss — Research Dossier

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Enicepatide is a once-weekly investigational peptide from Roche — a biased GLP-1/GIP dual receptor agonist that achieved up to 22.7% mean weight loss in Phase 2, with Phase 3 trials now underway and a triple-receptor combination trial (with the amylin analog petrelintide) on the horizon.

What is Enicepatide?

Enicepatide (investigational codes CT-388 and RO7795068) is a subcutaneous once-weekly peptide that simultaneously activates two receptors involved in metabolic regulation: the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR). Both receptors are part of the incretin hormone system, and dual activation of this pathway is the same mechanism as tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) — the first GLP-1/GIP dual agonist approved by the FDA for obesity.

Enicepatide was developed by Carmot Therapeutics using their Triple Peptide Chemotype Approach (TPCA) — a platform for engineering peptides that act on multiple metabolic receptors simultaneously. Roche acquired Carmot in December 2023 for approximately $2.7 billion, bringing CT-388 and other pipeline candidates into the Roche portfolio.

What distinguishes enicepatide from tirzepatide is its biased agonism profile: enicepatide is specifically engineered to minimize β-arrestin recruitment on both the GLP-1R and GIPR while preserving G-protein signaling. β-arrestin pathways mediate receptor internalization and may contribute to some adverse effects; designing a drug with reduced β-arrestin engagement — while maintaining the therapeutic G-protein-dependent activation — is a strategy aimed at sustained receptor activity and potentially improved tolerability.

As of November 2026, enicepatide has completed Phase 2 trials in both non-diabetic obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes, and Phase 3 registration trials (ENITH-1 and ENITH-2) are recruiting.

Mechanism of Action

Enicepatide acts as a biased dual agonist at GLP-1 receptors and GIP receptors. Here is what each receptor does in the context of obesity and metabolic health:

GLP-1 Receptor Agonism

  • Appetite suppression: GLP-1 is released by intestinal L-cells after eating; it signals to the hypothalamus and brainstem to reduce hunger and promote satiety
  • Insulin secretion: Glucose-dependent — stimulates pancreatic β-cells to release insulin when blood glucose is elevated
  • Glucagon suppression: Reduces post-meal glucagon, limiting hepatic glucose output
  • Gastric emptying: Slows gastric emptying, extending the satiety window after meals

GIP Receptor Agonism

  • Adipose tissue effects: GIP receptors are expressed on adipocytes; activation may enhance fat storage and mobilization in ways that complement GLP-1's central effects on satiety
  • Insulin potentiation: GIP is a potent insulin secretagogue, and its receptor agonism appears to amplify the metabolic improvements seen with GLP-1R agonism alone
  • Tolerability synergy: Evidence from tirzepatide's development suggests that adding GIPR agonism to GLP-1R agonism can maintain or improve weight loss efficacy while potentially improving gastrointestinal tolerability compared to pure GLP-1 mono-agonists at equivalent doses

Biased Agonism (Reduced β-arrestin)

Both GLP-1R and GIPR activate two main intracellular pathways when bound by an agonist: G-protein signaling (which drives most therapeutic effects — cAMP production, insulin secretion, satiety) and β-arrestin signaling (which mediates receptor internalization, desensitization, and some side effects). Enicepatide's reduced β-arrestin bias means more of its receptor binding translates to therapeutic G-protein signaling with less receptor downregulation — a potential advantage in sustained efficacy and tolerability. The clinical significance of this biased profile versus tirzepatide's profile has not yet been tested in a head-to-head trial.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 — Non-Diabetic Obesity

Results from the Phase 2 dose-finding trial in adults with overweight or obesity without type 2 diabetes:

  • Efficacy: Up to 22.7% mean weight loss at 48 weeks at the highest dose evaluated
  • Extreme responders: Approximately 26% of participants at the highest dose lost ≥30% of body weight — a threshold associated with near-surgical metabolic outcomes
  • Adverse events: Discontinuations due to adverse events were 5.9% (enicepatide) vs. 1.3% (placebo); adverse events predominantly GI-class and consistent with the incretin drug class
  • Safety profile: No unexpected safety signals identified in Phase 2

Phase 2 — Obesity + Type 2 Diabetes (Roche ad hoc release, September 22, 2026)

Results from the Phase 2 dose-finding trial in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes (N=447):

  • Weight loss: 15.5% mean weight loss at 48 weeks (highest 24 mg dose)
  • Glycemic control: Approximately 62% of participants achieved HbA1c below 5.7% — essentially achieving near-normal glycemia in a T2DM population; this is an extraordinary glycemic response rate
  • Safety: Well tolerated; no unexpected signals; GI-class adverse events consistent with drug class

Note: The difference between 22.7% weight loss in non-diabetic obesity and 15.5% in T2DM is consistent with established patterns in GLP-1-class drugs, where metabolic dysregulation in T2DM moderately attenuates weight-loss response. The glycemic benefit (62% HbA1c < 5.7%) makes the T2DM data especially compelling for a combined metabolic and weight-loss indication.

Phase 3 Program (ENITH-1 and ENITH-2)

  • ENITH-1: Phase 3 registrational trial in adults with overweight or obesity without T2DM (NCT07351045) — recruiting
  • ENITH-2: Phase 3 registrational trial in adults with overweight or obesity and T2DM (NCT07351058) — recruiting
  • Both trials are powered for regulatory approval; primary completion dates have not been publicly disclosed

ZYNERGY Combination Trial (Enicepatide + Petrelintide)

Roche and Zealand Pharma have planned the ZYNERGY Phase 2 combination trial (NCT07589686), evaluating enicepatide plus petrelintide (a once-weekly amylin analog) in adults with obesity. The trial was listed as "not yet recruiting" with an estimated start of November 2026. The triple-receptor logic (GLP-1R + GIPR + amylin receptor) mirrors Eli Lilly's EloraTZP program (eloralintide + tirzepatide) and targets additive satiety signaling across three mechanistically distinct neural and hormonal pathways.

Dosing in Research

Specific dosing details from the Phase 2 trials:

  • Route: Subcutaneous injection
  • Frequency: Once weekly
  • Highest Phase 2 dose (T2D trial): 24 mg per week (the dose achieving 15.5% weight loss and 62% HbA1c < 5.7%)
  • Dose selection for Phase 3: Not yet disclosed; Phase 3 ENITH trials will establish the registrational dose range
  • Important note: Enicepatide is investigational and not available outside of clinical trials. Research dosing information is provided for scientific context only and does not constitute guidance for personal use.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How does enicepatide differ from tirzepatide?

Both enicepatide (Roche/Carmot CT-388) and tirzepatide (Lilly, Mounjaro/Zepbound) are GLP-1/GIP dual receptor agonists, but they are distinct peptides with different molecular designs. The key pharmacological difference is biased agonism: enicepatide minimizes β-arrestin recruitment on both receptors, while tirzepatide has its own bias characteristics. Whether this translates to superior efficacy or tolerability in patients has not been tested in a head-to-head trial. Phase 2 efficacy numbers (enicepatide: 22.7% at 48 weeks; tirzepatide Phase 3: ~21% at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1) are not directly comparable due to different trial lengths, populations, and designs. Tirzepatide is FDA-approved for obesity and type 2 diabetes. Enicepatide is in Phase 3 — several years from potential approval.

Q: What is the ZYNERGY trial combining enicepatide with petrelintide?

ZYNERGY (NCT07589686) is a planned Phase 2 combination study of enicepatide plus petrelintide in adults with obesity. Enicepatide engages GLP-1R and GIPR (incretin pathways). Petrelintide engages amylin receptors in the brainstem area postrema — a mechanistically distinct satiety circuit with no overlap with the incretin pathway. Engaging all three receptor systems simultaneously could produce additive or synergistic weight loss beyond what any dual-receptor drug achieves. If, for example, enicepatide alone achieves ~22% weight loss and petrelintide alone achieves ~10%, a truly additive combination might approach 30-32% — the surgical weight loss range. This trial represents the same logic as Eli Lilly's EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) program. The trial is not yet underway; both drugs are investigational.

Q: When will enicepatide be approved and available?

Enicepatide is not approved anywhere as of November 2026. Phase 3 trials are recruiting but no completion dates have been disclosed. Typical Phase 3 obesity trials run 60–80+ weeks after full enrollment. A realistic timeline would be a potential NDA filing in 2028 at the earliest, with approval possibly in 2028–2029 — but this is speculative and depends on enrollment pace, interim efficacy, safety data, and regulatory review timelines. It will not be commercially available before approval, and it cannot be obtained outside of clinical trials before that point. The FDA-approved GLP-1/GIP option today is tirzepatide.

Research Limitations

  • Phase 2 data are company-reported from topline announcements; full peer-reviewed publications are pending
  • Phase 3 results (ENITH-1, ENITH-2) are needed for regulatory approval — Phase 2 efficacy does not guarantee Phase 3 success
  • No head-to-head trial against tirzepatide has been announced; efficacy comparison between the two GLP-1/GIP dual agonists is not established
  • No cardiovascular outcomes trial data available; long-term cardiovascular safety (beyond 48-week Phase 2 observation) is unknown
  • The 5.9% discontinuation rate due to adverse events (vs. 1.3% placebo) in the non-T2D Phase 2 warrants monitoring in Phase 3
  • ZYNERGY combination trial (enicepatide + petrelintide) has not yet started; triple-receptor combination benefit is theoretical at this stage
